+1 — hit the same thing this week. My AI coding agent traced the root cause
through the dev branch; it's a small fix, so posting details in case it helps
prioritize.

**Why links are dead today:**
1. Message markdown → `<a class="external-link">` via marked
   (`packages/ui/src/context/marked.tsx`).
2. DOMPurify (`packages/session-ui/src/components/markdown-cache.tsx`) strips
   `file:`/`vscode:` hrefs — the default `ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP` only keeps web
   schemes. Verified live against DOMPurify 3.4.12 with the repo's exact
   sanitize config.
3. The desktop click handler (`packages/desktop/src/renderer/index.tsx`)
   forwards everything to `shell.openExternal` via the `open-link` IPC, and
   the renderer origin is `oc://renderer`, so even schemeless absolute-path
   hrefs (`[x](/abs/path)`) resolve to garbage.

**Suggested implementation** — mindful of the link-hardening in #38914; this
deliberately does NOT route `file:` through `openExternal`:
1. Allow the `file` scheme in the sanitizer's `ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP`, only when
   `platform === "desktop"` (web keeps stripping it — browsers block `file:`
   anyway).
2. In the desktop click handler, branch on protocol: `file://` hrefs →
   `platform.revealPath(path)` / `platform.openPath(path)` — those IPC
   handlers already exist (`packages/desktop/src/main/ipc.ts`), already
   validate the target with `stat`, and already power the session header
   "Open in…" button. Everything else → `openLink` as today, keeping
   `shell.openExternal` http(s)-only per #38914.

Worth noting: clickable paths existed in the previous desktop app (see
#19144), so this is partially a regression from the rewrite. Also #17209 was
stale-bot-closed, not rejected.

I would also love to have this. In projects I see and use you usually have something like:
```
/parent
  /build
    compile_commands
  /src
    CMakeLists.txt
```

Or
```
/parent
  /src
    CMakeLists.txt
    /build
      compile_commands
```

I.e. the build folder is either a subdir of the parent or the source. In-source builds are widely discouraged so searching for compile_commands inside /src directly will likely turn up empty.

How about search for compile commands DB in all subfolders? Doesn't need to be recursively but I wouldn't hardcode the name. I've seen names like `__build__` to avoid clashes with "build" folders containing build-configuration files provided with the sources but not the actual build folder.

> I'd like to work on this. The root cause is clear: both `usage.ts` (L212) and `service.ts` (L653) hardcode `currency: "USD"` in the ACP `usage_update`. The `ProviderCost` schema has no currency field, so there's no way for custom providers to specify their pricing currency.
> 
> **Proposed fix:**
> 
> 1. Add optional `currency` field to `ProviderCost` in `provider.ts` (defaults to `"USD"` for backward compat)
> 2. Add `findCostCurrency()` utility to `usage.ts` (mirrors existing `findContextLimit()`)
> 3. Thread the currency through `sendUpdate` in both `usage.ts` and `service.ts`
> 4. Add test coverage for custom currency propagation

My PR #35877 fixes both by attaching a bounded stderr listener that captures the output for diagnostics instead of leaving it unread.

I can reproduce this with a newly reset OpenCode Go plan, so this does not appear to be exhausted account quota or a client temperature override.

I tested the Go endpoint directly using the same API key and a minimal payload:

- `kimi-k3`, `temperature` omitted: HTTP 429 — `Provider rate limit exceeded`
- `kimi-k3`, `temperature: 1`: HTTP 429 — `Provider rate limit exceeded`
- `kimi-k2.7-code`, `temperature` omitted: HTTP 200
- `mimo-v2.5`, `temperature` omitted: HTTP 200

The Kimi K3 requests did not include OpenCode-specific `mcp` or top-level `system` fields. Changing the Go API key also did not resolve it. This points to a stale or incorrect model-specific Kimi K3 rate-limit bucket/routing state on Console Go. The generic `Upstream request failed` message appears alongside or after the K3-specific 429 responses.

The issue is that opencode (like most TUI apps) captures mouse events, which blocks normal click-and-drag text selection.                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     To copy text from a TUI app:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     1. Hold Shift + click-and-drag to select text — this bypasses the TUI's mouse capture and lets the terminal handle selection                                                                                                                                                             
     2. Then Ctrl+Shift+C to copy (GNOME Terminal's copy shortcut)                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     This is the standard workaround for all terminal TUI apps (vim, htop, lazygit, etc.)
